title: Hindu Joint Family and Mitakshara Coparcenary

content.overview: A Hindu joint family is the wider unit of persons lineally descended from a common ancestor, their wives and unmarried daughters. The Mitakshara coparcenary is the narrower body of persons who acquire by birth an interest in joint family property. After the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, the daughter of a Mitakshara coparcener is a coparcener by birth in the same manner as a son (HSA s. 6). The karta manages the family and may alienate for legal necessity or benefit of the estate. Partition severs status and divides property.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Joint family or coparcenary? (2) Ancestral vs separate property? (3) Daughter’s birthright post-2005? (4) Karta’s power and necessity? (5) Partition?
content.study:
Joint family (wider) ≠ coparcenary (narrower birthright group). Post-2005 daughters are coparceners by birth under HSA s. 6. Karta’s alienation binds only if for legal necessity or benefit of the estate (or with consent). Dayabhaga does not recognise Mitakshara-type birthright coparcenary.

Case already in migrated file: Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 — daughter’s coparcenary by birth; right does not depend on father being alive on the amendment date; subject to statutory savings for earlier partitions/dispositions. No additional cases invented.

sections.heading: Joint family vs coparcenary
sections.body: Joint family is the wider social/legal unit; coparcenary is the birthright ownership group in Mitakshara law.

sections.heading: Daughter as coparcener (2005)
sections.body: Daughter of a Mitakshara coparcener is a coparcener by birth with the same rights and liabilities as a son (HSA s. 6).

sections.heading: Karta
sections.body: Manager of the joint family; may alienate joint family property for legal necessity or benefit of the estate.

sections.heading: Partition
sections.body: Severance of joint status and division of property; daughter as coparcener may claim equal share subject to s. 6 savings.

sections.heading: Dayabhaga contrast
sections.body: No Mitakshara-type birthright coparcenary; do not apply Mitakshara rules to Dayabhaga facts.

examples.title: Daughter as coparcener
examples.body: Father, son and daughter in Mitakshara family — daughter is coparcener by birth post-2005 and may claim equal share on partition subject to s. 6 savings.

examples.title: Alienation without necessity
examples.body: Karta sells joint family land without legal necessity or benefit — sale does not bind the challenging coparcener’s interest to that extent.

hypotheticals.question: Does a pre-2005 partition always bar a daughter’s claim?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only genuine partitions within the statutory savings as interpreted in Vineeta Sharma are protected; sham or incomplete partitions do not defeat the daughter’s rights.

distinctions.title: Joint family vs Mitakshara coparcenary
distinctions.left: Wider unit (lineal descendants, wives, unmarried daughters).
distinctions.right: Narrower birthright group in joint family property.

rows.right: Daughter of a coparcener is a coparcener by birth.

misconceptions.trap: Every Hindu family is automatically a Mitakshara coparcenary.
misconceptions.correction: Joint family is wider; not every joint family member is a coparcener.

misconceptions.trap: Daughter’s right depends on father being alive on 9 September 2005.
misconceptions.correction: Vineeta Sharma: right by birth; does not depend on father being alive on the amendment date, subject to statutory savings.

cases.name: Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma
cases.facts: Dispute over a daughter’s claim to coparcenary rights under the 2005 amendment and the effect of the father’s death and alleged earlier partitions.
cases.issue: Whether the daughter acquires coparcenary rights by birth only if the father was alive on the amendment date, and how statutory savings operate.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Daughter of a coparcener becomes a coparcener by birth in the same manner as a son. The right does not depend on the father being alive on the date of the amendment. Subject to statutory savings for partitions and testamentary dispositions before the cut-off; sham partitions do not defeat the right.
cases.holding: Daughter held entitled to claim as a coparcener; earlier conflicting decisions clarified.
cases.relevance: Binding authority on temporal operation of the 2005 amendment to HSA s. 6.
